name: diff
plain: `diff` shows exactly what differs between two files (or two folders): which lines were added, removed or changed.
It is how you see what a patch changes, what an attacker modified, or what differs between a backup and the current file.
when: Compare two versions of a config or source file.
Check which files differ between two folders.
Read a patch (the unified format is what git shows).

examples.title: Compare two files
examples.explain: Lines starting with < exist only in the first file, lines with > only in the second. Letters like 3c3 mean 'line 3 was changed'; a = added and d = deleted.

examples.title: Unified format  (-u)
examples.explain: Shows context with - and + lines, the format patches and git use. Add -U 5 for five context lines.

examples.title: Side by side  (-y)
examples.explain: Two columns with markers in the middle: | for a changed line, < and > for lines only on one side.

examples.title: Only say whether they differ  (-q, -s)
examples.cmd: diff -q a.txt b.txt; diff -s a.txt a.txt
examples.explain: -q reports just 'Files differ'; -s also tells you when they are the same.

examples.title: Compare folders  (-r)
examples.explain: Recursively lists which files differ or exist only on one side. Add -N to treat missing files as empty.

examples.title: Ignore whitespace and case  (-w, -b, -i)
examples.cmd: diff -w old.txt new.txt; diff -i a b
examples.explain: -w ignores all white space, -b ignores changes in the amount of white space, -i ignores letter case.

examples.title: Make a patch and apply it
examples.cmd: diff -u old.txt new.txt > fix.patch;  patch old.txt < fix.patch
examples.explain: The patch file records the changes; patch applies them. This is how fixes are shared in a defence challenge.

examples.title: Colour  (--color)
examples.explain: Colours removed lines red and added lines green in a terminal.

mistakes: Reading the arrows backwards: < is the first file, > the second.
diff exits with 1 when the files differ: in scripts that is not an error.
Comparing binaries with diff shows 'Binary files differ': use cmp or xxd.
Forgetting -r when comparing folders: diff old/ new/ without it only says 'Common subdirectories'.
